question: Eukaryotic organisms can have very complex functions to sustain themselves. At the cellular level, these involve several different types of chemical functions like energy production, metabolism etc. What are the membrane-bound structures called, which are present within the cell to keep each of these functionalities separate?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Organelles**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Organelles** are the membrane-bound structures within eukaryotic cells that compartmentalize various chemical functions.
 
• These structures include the **nucleus, mitochondria, endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi apparatus**, and others, each performing specific roles necessary for the cell's survival and functionality.
 
• By segregating different biochemical processes, organelles enhance the efficiency and regulation of cellular activities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The term "organelle" comes from the idea that these structures are to cells what organs are to the body.
 
• Each organelle has a unique structure that suits its specific function, such as the double membrane of mitochondria which supports its role in energy production.
 
• The study of organelles is crucial for understanding cell biology and the complex interactions that sustain life at the cellular level.
 
• Disruption in the function of any organelle can lead to cellular dysfunction and is associated with various diseases.
